text.p: Syria's parliament on Monday approved the country's 1997 budget which set expenditure at 211.125 billion Syrian pounds ($4.85 billion), officials said.
Revenues were projected at the same level as spending, but these included expected local and foreign borrowings.
Budget breakdowns were not made public, and the officials gave no figure for deficit before borrowing.
The budget, for the fiscal year from January 1, will be submitted to the president to become law.
Ministries have so far relied on temporary monthly allocations based on the 1996 budget, which set spending at 188.05 billion pounds, in accordance with a special presidential decree.
The 1997 budget earmarked 108.7 billion pounds for investment expenditure, while the rest was for current expenditure.
